extracted.intended_audience: DoD contracting officers, defense contractors, and acquisition/procurement compliance personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and contract clause requirements implementing DoD preference for United States vessels when transporting supplies by sea, including waiver grounds, documentation, definitions, reflagging/repair requirements, and enforcement remedies. Targets amendments to DFARS parts 242, 247, and 252 relevant to DoD acquisitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to transport supplies on U.S.-flag vessels (10 U.S.C. 2631(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 2631(a), DoD contractors shall transport supplies exclusively on U.S.-flag vessels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the baseline policy (247.572(a)). Applies to ocean transportation of supplies that are clearly identifiable for DoD use. Contracts should include clause 252.247-7023 (Transportation of Supplies by Sea) to implement this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver grounds for U.S.-flag requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD may waive the requirement when a U.S.-flag vessel (1) is not available at a fair and reasonable rate for commercial vessels of the United States; or (2) is not otherwise available (10 U.S.C. 2631(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors and subcontractors may request a waiver via the Contracting Officer by sufficiently explaining one of the two grounds. Contracting officers are delegated authority (Secretary of Defense delegations at 247.573(a)) to make availability determinations. Requests should be processed expeditiously; an unapproved DoD waiver prior to shipper's sailing date is not, by itself, a compensable delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation required to support waiver requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A documented description of current, diligent efforts made to secure U.S.-flag vessels, including points of contact (names and telephone numbers) with at least two U.S.-flag carriers contacted; copies of quotes will suffice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable documentation includes copies of quotes, telephone notes, emails, and other relevant communications. This requirement appears in clause 252.247-7023(e)(7) (and Alternates) and is required to demonstrate that U.S.-flag vessels are unavailable at a fair and reasonable rate or otherwise unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security-classified cargo requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts must provide for the use of vessels belonging to the United States when security classifications prohibit the use of other than vessels belonging to the United States (247.572(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where security classification restricts carriage, the contract should explicitly require vessels belonging to the United States regardless of other availability considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflagging or repair work requirement for time-charter vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: Any vessel used under a time charter contract for transportation of supplies shall have reflagging or repair work performed in the United States or its outlying areas if the work is performed on a vessel for which the contractor submitted an offer and prior to Government acceptance; corrective and preventive maintenance or repair work should be performed in the U.S. for the duration of the contract to the greatest extent practicable (10 U.S.C. 2631(c); 247.572(c); clause 252.247-7025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary of Defense may waive this requirement if critical to national security; DoD must immediately notify specified congressional committees when such a waiver is granted. The clause 252.247-7025 (Reflagging or Repair Work) prescribes the contractor obligations and definitions for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of domestic shipyard use in award evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: When obtaining carriage requiring a covered vessel, the contracting officer shall consider the extent to which offerors have had overhaul, repair, and maintenance work for covered vessels performed in shipyards located in the United States or Guam (section 1017 of NDAA 2007; 247.572(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an evaluative preference to encourage use of domestic shipyards; it affects source selection/evaluation by documenting prior domestic shipyard activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation preference for use of domestic shipyards (solicitation provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision 252.247-7026: Evaluation Preference for Use of Domestic Shipyards—Applicable To Acquisition of Carriage by Vessel for DOD Cargo in the Coastwise or Noncontiguous Trade (OCT 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provision establishes evaluation preferences in solicitations for carriage in coastwise/noncontiguous trade; it defines 'covered vessel' and other terms used to apply the preference. Use in solicitations per DFARS prescription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions that determine applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Key defined terms include: 'Covered vessel' (owned/operated/controlled by offeror and qualified for coastwise/noncontiguous trade under 46 U.S.C. provisions), 'U.S.-flag vessel' (vessel belonging to the United States or vessel of the United States as defined in 46 U.S.C. 116), 'Foreign-flag vessel' (any vessel not U.S.-flag), 'Ocean transportation' (water-borne transportation outside internal U.S. waters), 'Supplies' (items clearly identifiable for eventual DoD use), 'Reflagging or repair work', 'Corrective and preventive maintenance or repair', and 'Overhaul, repair, and maintenance work' (definitions at 247.571 and in clauses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions determine when clauses and statutory requirements apply (e.g., what counts as supplies, which vessels are covered). Contract language and applicability analyses should rely on these specific statutory/regulatory definitions to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract clause implementation and applicability (252.247-7023, -7025, -7026)
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule amends clauses and provisions at DFARS 252.247-7023 (Transportation of Supplies by Sea, including Alternates), 252.247-7025 (Reflagging or Repair Work), and 252.247-7026 (Evaluation Preference for Use of Domestic Shipyards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must insert the prescribed clauses and alternates in solicitations and contracts as required by the DFARS prescriptions; the rule clarifies certain paragraph language and removes unused/incongruent definitions. The rule does not impose new requirements on contracts at or below the SAT for commercial products (including COTS) and commercial services, but the clauses continue to apply where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting officer processing and remedies for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting officers shall exercise appropriate contractual rights and remedies against contractors who fail to comply; such remedies may include determination of ineligibility for future awards, termination of existing contracts, suspension or debarment, and consideration of equitable adjustment for unauthorized use of foreign-flag vessels (247.573(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting officers should also include information on contractor compliance with clause 252.247-7023 in past performance assessments (242.1502(g)(iii)). Remedies are discretionary and may be coordinated with legal and acquisition officials; evidence of unauthorized use may support equitable adjustment actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing timing and noncompensable delay rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer will process waiver requests as expeditiously as possible; however, if a DoD waiver is not approved prior to the shipper's sailing date, this will not of itself constitute a compensable delay under this or any other clause of the contract (252.247-7023(e) and Alternates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors should plan for possible denial/lack of timely waiver approval and cannot assume entitlement to delay costs simply because a waiver was pending at sailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on creating new DFARS certification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: 41 U.S.C. 1304 prohibits new certification requirements in the DFARS unless the certification is specifically imposed by statute or an approved justification exists for the certification. Therefore, DFARS will not add certification requirements (response to public comment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed substitutions of representations with certifications (e.g., in DFARS 252.242-7023 or 252.247-7025) are declined unless statutory authority or approved justification exists. Contract drafter should use representations where a certification would be prohibited.
